Hi Amit,
I hope you’re doing well.
We would like to sync with you on the next steps to enhance our custom DITAOT HTML5 output plugin and align on the best technical and delivery approach moving forward.
As background, as discussed previously, the following enhancements for the HTML5 plugin were identified:

ol.li: Search results mapped to the navigation tree
Highlighting matched search text in the content view
Advanced search options (Whole Word Only, Match Case)
PDF download option for parent + child topics

li.p: Breadcrumb navigation with cross-references
In addition, we also want to support the following:
Replacement of YUI 2 with a native TOC engine (CVEyui2-removal)

ul.li: From the highpriority items, our most immediate focus is item 5, followed by items2, 3, and 4.
For item 2 (highlighting matched search text), we have done some internal work already; however, we are not fully confident that the current approach is ideal or scalable.
For item 4 (prioritizing <title> content in search results), our understanding is that this may already be supported. We would appreciate it if you could confirm this.
For items 1 and 6, we plan to complete the implementation internally to manage budget. Some parts are already implemented, but they have not yet been extensively tested.
Item 8 (YUI 2 removal) has been implemented on our side and tested with a sample output, and the results look good so far. That said, we still need to extend testing across broader scenarios.

li.p: Our target is to have the priority items ready by the beginning of May, which makes it important for us to align early on scope, dependencies, and sequencing.

p.b: Advanced search (Whole Word Only, Match Case)

li.p: We would especially appreciate your input on the advanced search options.

Our understanding is that the current search implementation relies on stemmed words for indexing, with only the title and short description retained in their original (nonstemmed) form. Based on this, we are uncertain whether:

ul.li: The existing search architecture can realistically be extended to support whole word searches and case sensitivity, or
A new or significantly reworked search implementation would be required to properly support these capabilities.

li.p: We would value your assessment of whether the current approach is extendable or whether a redesign would be more appropriate, along with any recommendations you may have.

We are making some adaptations to the HTML5 plugin internally, while other parts will need to be implemented by your team. It’s important for us to sync up and agree on the best overall approach to proceed and ensure that our efforts align.

We would also like your guidance on the migration to DITA OT 4.x, particularly in relation to the requested feature enhancements. Our initial assumption is that the migration cannot be done fully in parallel with major feature adaptations, but we would like your input on this.
Specifically, we’d like to discuss:

ol.li: Whether it makes sense to migrate to DITA OT 4.x first before addressing the highpriority items, and whether this is feasible within our current timeline.
A rough estimate of the effort required to migrate the custom plugin to DITAOT 4.x.
If we continue working on the current DITAOT version in the short term, how much additional effort or technical risk this might introduce when migrating to 4.x later.
